chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and from his father Maymun who said:
We went out with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to the land of Tayba, and with him were Amr ibn Dinar and a group of his companions. We stayed in Tayba for as long as God willed.

Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rode upon a difficult camel. Amr ibn Dinar said to him: 'How difficult is your camel!' He said: 'Do you not know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Upon the peak of every camel is a satan, so disgrace it and subdue it, and mention the name of God upon it, for it is God Who carries'?
Then he entered Mecca and we entered with him without ihram.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram — the ritual state of pilgrim consecration (wearing special garments and observing restrictions)
key_terms.ذِرْوَة: Peak or hump — the highest point of a camel's back
key_terms.شَيْطَان: Satan — here representing the camel's obstinate or wild nature
key_terms.طِيبَة: Tayba — a blessed name for Medina, the city of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Baqir say about riding a difficult camel and remembering God's name?
ai.summary: Maymun ibn al-Qaddah narrates accompanying Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) on a journey from Medina to Mecca. When the Imam mounted a difficult camel, he cited a prophetic tradition that a satan perches on every camel's hump and commanded: subdue it, tame it, and invoke God's name over it, for God alone is the true carrier. The hadith closes with the notable detail that they entered Mecca without ihram, likely indicating an informal non-pilgrimage visit or a jurisprudential circumstance recognized by the Imam.
